clue.text: Ill-will shown about river nymph

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for ill-will goes round the river letter

parts.note: spite is ill-will

explanation.surface: Malice is displayed around a river spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a small fairy or elf, a spirit akin to a water nymph.

clue.text: One very quietly stands in line for sacking

indicators.note: stands in means is placed inside another word

parts.note: a string is a line
I is the Roman numeral one
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: A worker waits silently in a queue to be fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripping someone of a post is removing them from it, a form of dismissal.

clue.text: Ploughs back the profits

definitions.meaning: goes back over a furrow, turning again

explanation.definitionFit: A ploughman turns back at the headland, and an investment's yield is its gain.

clue.text: Attend here possibly to be given a warning

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone told to show up here or face the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: To be menaced with harm is to receive a warning of it.

clue.text: Transport in the soup?

parts.note: stock is a soup base, so a vehicle sitting in it is a car in stock; also a racing car that often ends up in trouble

explanation.surface: A vehicle somehow floating in a bowl of soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock car is a vehicle for racing, a form of transport, and stock is the liquid base of soup.

clue.text: "The ——— blade, Toledo trusty, for want of fighting was grown rusty" (Butler)

definitions.text: "The ——— blade, Toledo trusty, for want of fighting was grown rusty" (Butler)

parts.words: "The ——— blade, Toledo trusty, for want of fighting was grown rusty" (Butler)
parts.note: a quotation from Samuel Butler's Hudibras with the missing word describing a keen sword

explanation.surface: A line of verse about a sharp Spanish sword gone rusty.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank describes a blade that cuts keenly and incisively.

clue.text: The head requires personal cover

definitions.meaning: a headland jutting into the sea
a sleeveless cloak worn over the shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: A headland is a promontory, and a short cloak covers the wearer.

clue.text: Get rid of pollution and make lots of money!

explanation.definitionFit: To clear away mess is to tidy thoroughly, and making a killing financially uses the same phrase.

clue.text: Note the batch needs to be hardened again

parts.note: re is a note in the sol-fa scale
a set is a batch or group

explanation.surface: A memo about a batch that must be toughened once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete or jelly that sets again has hardened a second time.

clue.text: Marginal advantage

parts.note: a slight lead over rivals, and also the border of something

explanation.definitionFit: A slight lead over a rival is a small advantage, and a border is a margin.

clue.text: Private soldiers, anything but fresh

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers
being anything but fresh means being weary

explanation.surface: Ordinary soldiers who are worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like the rank of the soldiers but is the definition, meaning secluded.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired life is a private, secluded one.

clue.text: At one time reporters could be really speedy

parts.note: ex means former, from at one time
the press is the body of reporters

explanation.surface: Journalists of former days could work at great speed.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train or delivery is a very fast one.

clue.text: Coppers protecting royal person exhibit endurance

indicators.note: protecting means guarding by surrounding, so the coins go round the other pieces

parts.note: pence are copper coins
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen
a man is a person

explanation.surface: Police officers guarding a royal show staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but means copper coins, PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting endurance is the quality of being permanent.

clue.text: A flier in some difficulty

definitions.meaning: a wading bird of the sandpiper family
a tangle or problem, as in tying oneself up in one

explanation.definitionFit: The bird of that name is a flier, and a tangle is a difficulty or complication.

clue.text: Being doddery, need caring younger relation

indicators.note: being doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone frail needs looking after by a young relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's granddaughter is a relative of a younger generation.

clue.text: Rather stained material

indicators.note: material here suggests the letters are raw stuff to be worked into something new

explanation.surface: A preference for fabric bearing marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' reads as cloth that is stained, but signals reworking the letters of 'stained'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather, as in 'rather than', means in place of something else.

clue.text: Girl's seat is put out

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so the possessive gives DIS
to seat something is to place or locate it

explanation.surface: A young woman's chair has been moved aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint that is put out of place has been displaced.

clue.text: A duck kept inside stays fit

indicators.note: kept inside means one piece is held within another

parts.note: props and stays are both supports
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A duck is kept indoors and remains healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays fit' reads as remaining healthy, but 'stays' is PROPS and 'fit' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means relevant or suitable to the matter in hand, so fitting.

clue.text: Slightly damaged, so withdrawn

definitions.meaning: taken out of a race or competition

explanation.definitionFit: A light graze marks a surface, and a horse pulled from a race is struck off the card.

clue.text: They're stony, but have rent and gas to cope with

indicators.note: to cope with suggests handling and working the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hard-hearted who still has rent and gas bills to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnets are gemstones, so stony things.

clue.text: Though a little eccentric, he's the most prosperous

indicators.note: a little means only part of the run of words is used, a stretch tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A rather odd man who is also the wealthiest.
explanation.definitionFit: The wealthiest person is the most prosperous.

clue.text: A port of greater acidity

definitions.meaning: the Moroccan harbour city on the Strait of Gibraltar

explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a Moroccan port city, and something more tart in flavour is tangier.

clue.text: Repeat a trite broadcast on English

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Airing a stale line again on English radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or do something again is to repeat it.

clue.text: Hose needs a violent blow with the fist

definitions.meaning: hose is an old word for stockings or legwear

definitions.text: a violent blow with the fist

explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery includes stockings, and slang for a punch is the same word.

clue.text: A beast has to give way always

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: An animal that must always yield.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullock raised for beef is a beast of the farm.

clue.text: Many a fellow holding on can appear uncertain

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the first pair of pieces wraps round the second

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a gent is a fellow
taken as written
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A crowd of men grasping a can look unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contingent depends on chance, so it is not yet sure.

clue.text: The person making 13's rank

definitions.meaning: one who ties the answer to 13 across
a row or level in a series

explanation.definitionFit: One who ties is so named, and a row in a stack of seats is a level.

clue.text: A case of pins and needles

definitions.text: A case of pins and needles

parts.words: A case of pins and needles
parts.note: a small sewing box, not the tingling sensation

explanation.surface: A bout of tingling limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: This small ornamental container holds sewing items like needles.

clue.text: Settle on Burlington House for a Greek heroine's presentation

parts.note: to elect is to choose or settle on
Burlington House in London is the home of the Royal Academy, RA

explanation.surface: Choosing a London gallery to stage a classical drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House on Piccadilly in London houses the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles and Euripides each wrote a tragedy named for this daughter of Agamemnon, a staging of her story.

clue.text: A means of making pupils come clean!

definitions.text: A means of making pupils come clean!

parts.words: A means of making pupils come clean!
parts.note: pupils are the centres of the eyes, not schoolchildren confessing

explanation.surface: A method to get schoolchildren to own up.
explanation.definitionFit: This small cup is used to rinse the eye, washing the pupil.

clue.text: . Tradesman appealed to by a trio of little creatures lacking vision?

definitions.text: Tradesman appealed to by a trio of little creatures lacking vision?

parts.words: Tradesman appealed to by a trio of little creatures lacking vision?
parts.note: the three blind mice of the nursery rhyme lost their tails, so they would want someone to give tails back

explanation.surface: Three blind mice seek help from a shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the three blind mice have their tails cut off by the farmer's wife; read as RE-TAILER, a shopkeeper restores them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling goods to the public is a tradesman.

clue.text: Saw the governor beginning to languish in retirement

indicators.note: in places the governor and the first letter inside the word for retirement

parts.note: going to bed is retiring for the night
HE is His Excellency, the title of a governor

indicators.note: this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: Seeing the governor start to fade once he has retired.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, to see or observe.
